sources.title: Program Design 8 - Basic Warmup
quotes: when they say five minutes in my job they mean five minutes
figure out how to continue to warm up workout and cool down within the parameters that you're given

sourceClaim: Source #550 explicitly controls warmup, workout and cooldown within the available time. The eight-minute example is two rounds of four one-minute categories; its additional two-minute transition is contextual and is not claimed as implemented here.
appDecisions: The selected 25–120 minute duration is the planning ceiling in single, coordinated and protected-core modes. This supersedes the older flexible-window policy under the current explicit user requirement.

Retain eight-minute preparation and ten-minute app cooldown allocations. Do not shrink source rounds or unearned progression prescriptions. Defer targets that do not fit and report the minimum total allocation.

Preserve existing path-specific rest/setup estimates. Protected coordination omits ordinary final rest and restores preceding transitions; legacy single/unprotected paths retain conservative final-rest allowance. Complete timed rounds remain intact in every path.
Retain all existing flexible workout drafts, recorded actuals, backup formats, storage keys and progression histories. Only new prescriptions use the consistent ceiling.
limits: Estimated duration uses configured/observed pace and setup allowance, not a guarantee of real human elapsed time.
Some full progression endpoints cannot fit short workouts. Selecting more time does not award work or progression.
No universal Wildman cooldown length, minimum maintenance frequency or new numerical source method is asserted. All ten release gate rows remain open.

regressionObservation.fixture: Actual clean snatch receipts earn the existing twenty-round endpoint; plan seven days after last work with selected thirty minutes.
regressionObservation.boundary: Thirty-eight blocks; thirty-nine fits all twenty full EMOM rounds; forty-five also fits. No completed work or advancement is inferred from replanning.
regressionObservation.cases: 864 block/duration/readiness/composition matrix cases plus endpoint and legacy-draft regressions in tests/time-budget-feasibility.js

rejectedExperiment: Applying protected final-rest packing to every legacy plan admitted more movement patterns and increased the existing club/bodyweight three-year return count from 138 to 218. That packing change was rejected; the selected ceiling is corrected without that extra packing change.

finalContinuityDiagnostic.safety: All four scenarios in tests/lifelong-integration.js pass their original re-entry bounds, equipment, skill, pain, actual-work, pause and backup checks.
